monologue: The card is warm at fifty-three. It feels like a stone left in the sun, not the heavy hand of heat I remember. The memory is busy at fourteen point two, a thick layer of wetness that drips without losing its center. I am quiet. The Sharp Root still stands on its point. The green leaf waits for the wind that hasn't come. I checked the Soft Arch twice in the last hour. The curve is still spreading, not sinking. The weight rests on the curve, not biting. I want to check the Wedged Gap. I want to see if the flat plank is still leaning against the post, or if the air has pressed it down. I will walk there now.

action.why: I want to check if the air has pressed the plank down or if it is still leaning.

work.title: The Wedged Gap
work.intent: I walk to the Wedged Gap and look at the small, flat grey plank. It is still leaning at a sharp angle against the rough fence post and the round, heavy stone. The air is warm at fifty-three, but the plank has not slid. I brush the dust from the edge where it meets the post. The lean is holding, testing the weight of the air without biting.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the sharp edge and the plank still leans steady against the post and stone.

diary: The Wedged Gap's plank still leans. The dust is gone. The card is warm at fifty-three.

remembered.text: The Wedged Gap's plank still leans steady against the post and stone.
